details.label: Discussion
details.text: MRMS echo tops and lightning counts have been steadily declining within the eastern half of an MCS across southern WV and into western VA as the squall line continues to migrate into a more cool/stable environment. The severe threat from this portion of the line should continue to steadily decline with the coming onset of nocturnal cooling. Heading into the evening hours, the severe threat should remain concentrated across western portions of the MCS over southern KY and into east/northeast TN. Here, downstream temperatures remain in the low to mid 80s with MLCAPE values near 2000 J/kg, and forcing along the outflow boundary will continue to promote additional thunderstorm development with some attendant damaging wind threat for at least the next couple of hours. However, the downstream KMRX VWP is currently sampling somewhat weaker deep-layer wind shear compared to other locations further upstream prior to the MCS passage. This suggests that the line may become increasingly outflow dominant. Additionally, the coming onset of nocturnal cooling should also contribute to a gradual weakening trend beyond roughly 01 to 02 UTC, which appears to be reflected well by recent HRRR/RRFS time-lagged solutions

mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: A large hail threat may continue with supercells across parts of western Nebraska this evening. Watch issuance is possible

details.label: Summary
details.text: A large hail threat may continue with supercells across parts of western Nebraska this evening. Watch issuance is possible

details.label: Discussion
details.text: A long-lived supercell that has a history of producing large to very large hail across southwest SD is tracking southeastward, and should move into parts of the NE Panhandle/western NE in the next hour or so. Other convection is also ongoing along and perhaps just east of a weak surface boundary draped across western NE. Latest mesoanalysis estimates some lingering MLCIN across this region, which is evidenced by updrafts struggling to be sustained with southward extent in western NE. Still, some risk for large hail may continue with the well-established supercell moving southeastward out of southwest SD, as deep-layer shear remains strong. Trends are being monitored for possible watch issuance, with overall coverage of severe convection remaining uncertain
